_comment: Search parameters. Edit freely - find_jobs.py reads this every run. Personal values (addresses, salary thresholds) come from environment variables, never this file.
_retuned: 2026-08-17: retuned to the 2026-08-16 resume rebuild. Analytics dropped, warehouse_systems added as the lead path, targeting raised to Director/Senior Manager, geography moved from a flat allow-list to core/relocate/passion tiers.

candidate._comment: Real thresholds arrive as COMP_FLOOR / COMP_TARGET env vars (GitHub secrets). These defaults are placeholders.
candidate._hard_filters_comment: These drop roles from the report entirely rather than just demoting their score. A role is only dropped on evidence: the detail page must have been fetched and read. Anything unread is held back for the next run, never silently discarded. The travel ceiling is load-bearing for the 2026-08-16 SAP reframe - Big-4 functional practice roles are the 40-80% travel ones, and this is what actually removes them.

geo_tiers._comment: Tiered geography, 2026-08-17. core = no move required. relocate = Dan would move for a strong offer, so these are included but FLAGGED so the cost is visible. passion = only worth a move for the right kind of role, so each city is gated by matched path OR employer. Anything not matching a tier is excluded.

core._states_comment: Hybrid and on-site in Denver are INCLUDED on purpose - Dan likes an office.

relocate._comment: Atlanta is the strongest core-career option (Manhattan Associates, plus Home Depot / UPS / Coca-Cola / Delta supply chain; GA roots). San Diego secondary.

passion._comment: Gated: a role here must match one of the gate's paths OR one of its employers. The employer allowlist is not redundant - a title like 'Technical Program Manager, Studio Technology' classifies as product_program under longest-match, so a path-only gate would exclude exactly the roles that make these cities worth considering.

gates.note: F1 / motorsport host cities - motorsport roles only
Los Angeles - media / film business and technology side only, never creative

warehouse_systems.label: Warehouse / supply-chain systems leadership
warehouse_systems.note: LEAD path (2026-08-16). Closest match to what Dan does today and the highest conversion. Résumé variant: warehouse-systems. Note the signal split against ops_leadership: 'warehouse management system' and 'wms' belong here, bare 'warehouse management' / 'warehouse manager' / 'warehouse operations' belong to ops_leadership. classify_path() resolves the overlap by longest match, so keep the long forms here and the short forms there.

product_program.label: Product / technical program management
product_program.note: Co-lead path (2026-08-16). Dan manages product owners, owns a live backlog, and holds sole UAT-start and production sign-off - which closes the credibility gap POSITIONING.md used to flag here. Opens the tech sector, where equity lifts total comp. Résumé variant: product-program.

sap_erp.label: SAP / ERP program + deployment (business side)
sap_erp.note: Business-side ONLY. Dan was the business expert directing matrixed IBM/SAP functional consultants - he does not want and would not win functional-consultant or Big-4 practice roles. Site readiness, cutover, and deployment are ERP-deployment signals and stay here, NOT in warehouse_systems. Enforcement is three-layered: no magnet keywords, explicit rejects in seniority.reject, and employer_penalties for the Big-4 - plus the travel ceiling, which does most of the work. Résumé variant: sap-erp.
sap_erp._signal_length_comment: The multi-word forms are mandatory, not redundant. classify_path() resolves by LONGEST match, so bare 'sap' (3 chars) loses to product_program's 'program manager' (15) - which sent every 'SAP Program Manager', Dan's single most common target title, into the wrong path until this was caught in testing 2026-08-17.

ops_leadership.label: Operations / supply chain leadership
ops_leadership._weight_comment: 0.8, not 0.7: at 0.7 a Denver Director of Operations scores 6.8 against a 7.0 report threshold, which silences the fallback path completely rather than merely ranking it last.
ops_leadership.note: FALLBACK (2026-08-16) - held in reserve, not a primary push, hence the lowest weight. Also the base to re-angle for sports/entertainment operations. Owns the bare warehouse/ops title forms; the systems forms belong to warehouse_systems. Résumé variant: operations.

motorsport.label: F1 / motorsport
motorsport.note: Passion path. Thin volume, lower comp - surface anything that appears. Weight deliberately matches the lead path so a rare F1 role tops the day's list (confirmed intentional 2026-08-17). Liberty Media, which owns F1, is HQ'd in Englewood CO - so these roles can clear CORE geography with no relocation. See company_path_fallback: Liberty Media corporate titles carry no motorsport signal and would otherwise be dropped before scoring.

media_entertainment.label: Media / entertainment (business + technology side)
media_entertainment.note: Passion path, added 2026-08-17 so the LA geography gate has something to gate on. Business and technology side only - program, product, systems, and operations roles at studios and streamers. NEVER creative or production-craft roles. Deliberately excludes a bare 'business operations' signal: it would vacuum up generic BizOps roles nationwide, and the LA gate's employer allowlist already covers the TPM-at-a-studio case.

company_path_fallback._comment: When classify_path() finds no title signal, fall back to the employer. Liberty Media posts corporate/commercial roles out of Englewood CO whose titles carry no motorsport signal at all - without this they get matched_path=None and are dropped before scoring, which would hide Dan's most reachable F1 opportunity, the one needing no move. domain_bonus cannot do this job: it only applies AFTER a path is assigned.

seniority._comment: Tiered 2026-08-17 to target Director and Senior Manager. Scored by LONGEST matching term, so 'Associate Manager' does not score as 'manager'. The IC penalty stacks on top of the best positive tier: an IC title lands below report.min_score_to_report in practice but is never hard-rejected, so the call stays reversible and nothing is written to seen.json as settled.

employer_penalties._comment: Score penalty, not a hard drop (2026-08-17). The sap-erp reframe is business-side only, never Big-4 functional practice - but a legitimate non-consulting role at one of these firms should still be visible, just not near the top. Matched against the employer name only, with word boundaries. The travel ceiling in candidate.hard_filters removes most of these outright; this is the backstop for the ones that post under 50%.

domain_bonus._comment: Matched with word boundaries. 'companies' is checked against the employer name only; 'title_words' against the job title only. Keep both specific - generic words like 'media' or 'film' produced garbage matches (Thin Films, Enterprise Media) on the first run.

workday._comment: Verified 2026-08-17: 41 open reqs. Manhattan Associates is the WMS vendor POSITIONING.md names as the strongest Atlanta option.

direct_career_sites._comment: Non-standard ATSs with no public JSON API - checked by the /job-feed skill via WebSearch/WebFetch, NOT by the script. Every org here was probed against Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, and the obvious Workday tenants on 2026-08-17 and returned 404; they are on SuccessFactors, iCIMS, or custom stacks. Do not re-probe these three ATSs for them - the result is recorded, not unknown. Anything that later gets a working endpoint should move into target_boards.
sites: Liberty Media / FOM - libertymedia.com/careers + formula1.com/en/careers (Englewood CO HQ; highest-value manual check)
Las Vegas GP / Miami GP / COTA (Austin) - event organizations, seasonal

report._enrich_comment: Comp and travel are now hard filters, so anything past this cap is held for the next run rather than reported unchecked. Keep it above a normal day's kept count.

email._comment: Addresses arrive as EMAIL_TO / EMAIL_FROM env vars (GitHub secrets); password as EMAIL_PASSWORD. Nothing personal is stored in this file.
